text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kresimir Zubak, Croat member of collective presidency, says investigation by international police into Mostar incident is incomplete because it fails to discuss events that led to the February clash.
- A $500,000 World Bank project will help repair natural gas network over the next five years.
- Chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency Alija Izetbegovic accepts results of investigation conducted by the international police monitors into violent incident in Mostar this month.

- Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson discussed with Bosnian authorities establishment of Bosnia's central bank and common currency, education and repatriation of refugees living in Sweden during his first visit to Sarajevo.
- Diner's Club branch from Zagreb will offer credit cards in Bosnia after signing a contract on partnership with Bosnia's Privredna bank.

- Phillip Morris held talks with Sarajevo's tobacco factory on reviving production which was disrupted by 1992-1995 war. Before the conflict, the tobacco factory manufactured 2,400 tons of cigarettes a year.
